Marie Curie PhD vacancy (DC8) for PhD research titled "Additive manufacturing of ceramics with complex surfaces for small-scale turbomachinery"
description: The PhD research will be carried out in the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy team at the Department of Materials Engineering of KU Leuven. KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a center of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. The university caters to over 60,000 students from more than 140 countries. KU Leuven's three doctoral schools provide internationally oriented PhD tracks for more than 4,000 doctoral students. KU Leuven and affiliated knowledge institutes provide fertile ground for innovation and high-tech entrepreneurship in the Leuven region. This favorable climate for knowledge-driven innovation makes the Leuven region an attractive location for many high-tech companies. KU Leuven website: https://www.kuleuven.be/english/kuleuven/ Project KU Leuven seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded, four-year international doctoral position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) project TURBO-IMPACT (TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology ; Website: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350). The TurboImpact project, funded by Horizon Europe – MSCA-DN, tackles challenges in designing, optimizing, selecting materials, and manufacturing small-scale turbomachinery for applications in heat pumps, fuel cells, organic Rankine cycles, or gas turbines. This project develops robust system and component design methods, an integrated manufacturing platform, and multi-material joining techniques to efficiently produce small-scale turbomachinery. In this EU project, this PhD researcher (DC8) will focus on the complete indirect DLP/SLA additive manufacturing route for silicon nitride turbomachinery components. This involves the development of a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry, optimization of DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components such as impellers, and the post-printing debinding and sintering process to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components. The AM parts will be microstructurally, mechanically and geometrically characterized. Simple geometries will be used for the evaluation of joining and machining performances, whereas the complex near-net-shaped components will be applied in turbomachinery. The Doctoral Candidate Will Develop a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry and optimize DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components Realize post-printing debinding and sintering processes to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components Elucidate the processing – microstructure – mechanical properties – geometrical accuracy correlations. The project includes potential international secondments at EPFL (Switzerland), Admatec Additive Solutions (The Netherlands) and IFW (Germany). The researcher is supervised by Prof. Jozef Vleugels (https://www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/nl/person/00006337), head of the Functional Materials Division (FUNMAT) and coordinator of the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy research group at the Department of Materials Engineering. The research group has a long track record (>35 years) on the powder metallurgical development, processing and characterisaton of ceramics, cermets, metcers and metals. More information on the website (https://www.mtm.kuleuven.be/english/research/siem/ACPM) Profile I have a two-year master degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, or an equivalent master degree. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses, master thesis or prior professional activities, I have gathered basic experience on the processing of ceramics, additive manufacturing, microstructural and mechanical characterization or I have a profound interest in these topics. I demonstrate a strong sense of initiative and responsibility, while also being an effective and collaborative team player. I am very motivated and obtained good grades (minimum distinction level) I feel comfortable to work as a team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and be inspired by my colleagues. Special requirements: In accordance with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network regulations: Applicants must comply with the MSCA Mobility Rule. At the time of recruitment, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the hiring Country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment. Applicants must be doctoral candidates (i.e., not already hold a doctoral degree) and be eligible under the MSCA Doctoral Network rules at the time of recruitment Short stays such as holidays, compulsory national service, or time spent as part of a refugee procedure are not considered. Applicants must have a two-year master's degree in Materials Engineering, Materials Science, or an equivalent master degree , or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Offer Successful Candidates Will Be enrolled in the KU Leuven PhD programme, Conduct research in a stimulating international environment with access to state-of-the-art facilities and supervision by recognised experts Participate in local and network-wide training activities aimed at advancing scientific knowledge and transferable skills, Attend workshops and international conferences relevant to their research topic, Undertake secondments of approximately 4–6 months at other network or associated partner institutions. Receive further doctoral training for PhD candidates in the framework of the KU Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School (https://set.kuleuven.be/phd), known for its strong focus on both future scientists and scientifically trained professionals who will valorise their doc

title: Ingénieur(e) calcul en mécanique des structures expérimenté(e) F/H
description: Travaillant au sein de l’équipe « Technology » de l’ingénierie Produit, l’ingénieur(e) calcul en intégrité mécanique réalise des analyses statiques, dynamiques et thermomécaniques sur les composants et assemblages des produits nucléaires. Ces produits incluent notamment la turbine à vapeur, l’alternateur, les pompes, les échangeurs de chaleur et leurs systèmes auxiliaires. Le rôle comprend également la contribution au développement et à l’amélioration des méthodes et outils dédiés aux analyses d’intégrité mécanique, afin de garantir la fiabilité et la performance des équipements. Les missions clés : Réaliser des analyses d’intégrité mécanique par la méthode des éléments finis sur des composants, conformément aux critères de dimensionnement et aux règles et instructions internes. Modéliser des structures complexes à l’aide du logiciel de maillage HyperMesh et effectuer des simulations par éléments finis sous ANSYS. Personnaliser les modèles, automatiser les cas de charge et effectuer des post-traitements avancés à l’aide du langage APDL (Ansys Parametric Design Language). Réaliser des analyses statiques et dynamiques (modales, sismiques, harmoniques, transitoires), ainsi que des études de durée de vie (fatigue, nocivité, propagation de fissures). Effectuer des calculs mécaniques linéaires et non linéaires (non-linéarités de contact, de comportement matériau et de géométrie). Intégrer les exigences des codes (CODAP, EN 13445, ASME, RCC-M) dans les études de dimensionnement des appareils à pression.
